data.meta_description: Need a licence to charter a yacht in Marbella? 2029 rules explained for non-Spanish visitors. No licence needed for skippered charters. Book your trip today.
data.summary: Understand the 2029 licence requirements for yacht charter in Marbella. Most visitors don't need a licence when booking a skippered charter; this guide explains the rules for bareboat and private skippers.
key_facts: No licence required for skippered charters from Puerto Banús.
Bareboat charter (self-drive) requires a valid ICC or RYA Day Skipper.
Spanish law: recreational craft under 24m can be skippered without a licence if the skipper is paid.
Non-EU licence holders may need a translation or international permit for bareboat hire.

faq.q: Do I need a licence to charter a yacht in Marbella in 2029?
faq.a: No, if you book a skippered charter – which is what we offer. Spanish law requires a professional skipper on any commercial charter. You don't need any licence or previous experience. For bareboat charters (self-drive), you'd need an ICC or RYA Day Skipper, but we only provide skippered boats.

faq.q: What licence is needed for a bareboat charter in Spain?
faq.a: For bareboat charter in Spain, you need an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or a recognised equivalent like the RYA Day Skipper. Non-EU licence holders may need an official translation or an International Driving Permit for pleasure craft. Always check with the charter company before booking.

faq.q: Can I drive a charter boat without a licence in Marbella?
faq.a: Only if you book a skippered charter. The licensed skipper handles navigation and docking. You can still take the helm under their supervision – many guests enjoy steering for a few minutes – but legally the skipper remains responsible. Self-drive without a licence is not permitted.

faq.q: Are there any changes to licence rules in 2029?
faq.a: No major changes are expected for 2029. Spanish maritime regulations for recreational charter remain stable: skippered charters require no licence from guests, bareboat charters require an ICC. Always verify with local authorities or your charter operator before travelling.

faq.q: What if I have a UK or US boating licence?
faq.a: UK-issued RYA qualifications (Day Skipper, Coastal Skipper) are widely accepted in Spain. US licences (e.g. USCG Captain's licence) may need an ICC or a certified translation. For peace of mind, book a skippered charter – no licence needed at all.

faq.q: Do I need a licence for a jet ski or tender?
faq.a: Jet skis and tenders on our charters are operated only by the licensed skipper. Guests cannot drive them independently. The Mangusta 80 charter includes a jet ski, but it's for the skipper's use. If you want to drive a jet ski yourself, you'd need a specific PWC licence.

faq.q: Is a VHF radio licence required for charter boats?
faq.a: For skippered charters, no – the skipper holds the necessary VHF licence (e.g. SRC). Guests don't need one. For bareboat charter, a VHF licence is typically required alongside the ICC. Again, with our boats, you're covered.

faq.q: What documents do I need to bring for a skippered charter?
faq.a: Just a valid passport or ID card. No boating licence, no certificates. We recommend bringing sunscreen, a hat, and swimwear. The skipper handles all paperwork and safety briefings.

data.body_html:
Planning a yacht charter in Marbella and wondering about licence rules for 2029? The good news: if you book a skippered charter – which is what we offer – you don't need any licence at all. Spanish law requires a professional skipper on board for commercial charters, so you just relax. This guide covers the 2029 requirements, what's changed (spoiler: not much), and how to stay legal on the Costa del Sol.

Do you need a licence for a Marbella yacht charter in 2029?

No. For skippered charters – the standard model in Puerto Banús and Marbella Marina – guests never need a licence. The skipper holds the necessary qualifications (Spanish Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo or equivalent). You simply show up, board, and enjoy. This applies to all our boats, from the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) to the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax).

Bareboat vs skippered: what's the difference?

Bareboat charter means you rent the vessel without crew – you are the skipper. For that, Spanish law requires an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or a recognised equivalent (e.g. RYA Day Skipper). Non-EU licence holders may need a translation or International Permit. But we only offer skippered charters, so you never deal with bareboat paperwork.

What licence do skippers need in Marbella?

Our skippers hold Spanish recreational licences (PER or Patrón de Yate) or equivalent international qualifications. They are experienced with local waters – from the Marbella coastline to Cala del Faro and Estepona. They handle navigation, safety, and docking. You can take the wheel under supervision, but legally the skipper remains responsible.

2029 rule changes: what's new?

As of 2029, Spanish maritime regulations remain stable. No major changes are expected for recreational charter. The key points: skippered charters require no guest licence; bareboat charters require ICC or RYA. Always verify with your charter operator – we confirm requirements at booking. For now, the rules are clear and simple.

What about jet skis and tenders?

Jet skis and tenders on our charters (e.g. the free jet ski on the Mangusta 80) are operated only by the licensed skipper. Guests cannot drive them independently. If you want to drive a jet ski yourself, you'd need a specific PWC licence – not included in a standard charter. Stick to the main boat and let the skipper handle the toys.

Documents you need for a skippered charter

Just a valid passport or ID card. No boating licence, no certificates, no VHF radio licence. We recommend bringing sunscreen, a hat, and swimwear. The skipper handles all paperwork and safety briefings. For groups, a list of passenger names may be required – we'll ask in advance.

Which boats are available with a skipper?

All of them. From the Azimut 39 (€749/2h) to the Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h with jet ski), every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT. No hidden costs. Here's a quick overview:

Great – you can still book a skippered charter and take the helm under supervision. Many guests enjoy steering for a few minutes. If you want to charter bareboat in the future, your ICC or RYA will be valid in Spain. For now, just relax and let our skipper handle the work.
